text_blocks.snippet: Active scams targeting Central Illinois include fake local service listings, government and municipal impersonations, and fraudulent text message alerts.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake local service listings, government and municipal impersonations, and fraudulent text message alerts

list.snippet: Fake Garage Door Repair: Con artists set up fake online listings or spoof trusted local business names, showing up in unmarked vehicles to drastically inflate repair bills (turning a $700 job into a $2,200 charge). <Quote>“two Central Illinois women say they called a listing believing it was a garage door service but the people who showed up were not the company they expected a $700 repair turned into a $2,200 bill.”, as noted by [25 News](https://www.facebook.com/25NewsWEEK/videos/a-700-garage-door-repair-turned-into-a-2200-bill-for-two-local-women-after-they-/1750619759468452/).</Quote>

Storm Chaser Fraud: Door-to-door solicitors target neighborhoods after severe weather, offering quick home or roof repairs, demanding large cash deposits upfront, or posing as FEMA/state-certified agents. <Quote>“Damaging storms draw scammers looking to exploit as communities rebuild.”, according to [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/illinois-ag-warns-scammers-targeting-repairs-storms/).</Quote>

Fake City Invoices: Fraudsters send phony letters and invoices on counterfeit official letterhead—specifically targeting residents who recently appeared before local zoning boards, such as in Pekin. <Quote>“The Pekin Police Department is warning residents that scammers are attempting to impersonate city departments.”, reported by [Central Illinois Proud](https://www.centralillinoisproud.com/news/local-news/pekin-police-warning-scam/).</Quote>
DMV and Tollway Text Scams: Phishing texts falsely claim recipients owe money for unpaid traffic tickets, tolls, or face driver's license suspension, directing users to malicious payment links.
Package Delivery Texts: Fraudulent SMS messages claiming to be from the USPS or UPS use missing address pretexts to steal credit card data.
